Puspokladany Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Püspökladány, Hungary

Not demolished. Established in 1870, this cemetery's roughly 50 to 70 surviving tombstones sit beside Püspökladány's Christian cemetery. The Jewish community here traces to a lone tavern lessee recorded in an 1754 census, but only grew substantially after 1856, when infrastructure improvements to the town drew settlers and the community won permission to worship publicly; it peaked at 574 people by 1900 and supported a mikveh, a yeshiva, and its own steam mill. Eighty-seven Jewish men from the town died serving in the Hungarian army during WWI. In June 1944, the community — along with those of two neighboring towns — was deported to the Debrecen Ghetto; the 50 to 60 survivors who returned afterward had all left again by the 1950s.
